items.title: Ed Allen Interview, 1961-01-14
items.q: He said, Al, I got a record tomorrow. I said, what you're going to make? ... He called me anything next morning, as long as I went on the record.

ctx.x: The songs that Clarence Williams recorded were mostly his own songs?

Mostly all his own songs. So he'd make up some nights, we'd sit up and make them up overnight, but I'm going to make it. He said, Al, I got a record tomorrow. I said, what you're going to make? He said, I don't know. How does it sound? Blue, blue, blue, blue, blue. I said, sounds all right. He said, well, let's do the part. I'm going to make some more naked. I better make it with the next, put some name on it, and make it in the next three or four weeks, a month or two, he decided to publish it and put it out. A…

Yeah. Secretary, arrangers, and he had different people coming in the range, like nobody else. You said he had somebody from his office that once made a record? Yeah, one time we had one of these things, I don't remember,
